questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

A slap on the wrist

options.text: Beating someone too much on the wrist.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **A very mild punishment.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom **"A slap on the wrist"** is** A very mild punishment.**
 
• Therefore **option 3 **is a correct option.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's discuss about idioms:
 
• ​A group of words established by usage as having a meaning not deducible from those of the individual words.​​
 
 
• For example:- 
 
 
• **On cloud nine** - Being very happy.
 
• **Get your act together** - Get organized and do things effectively.
 
• **Back against the wall **- Stuck in a difficult circumstance with no escape.

I hope it will not __put you out__ if I am late.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **(3) **irritate you.

• The given idiom **'put someone out'** means 'upset or annoy someone.' (किसी को परेशान करना)

 
 
• *Example - It is a very sociable diet to follow because you don't have to **put anyone out**.*
 
 
 
• The word ** irritate** means 'to make somebody angry; to annoy' (किसी को नाराज़ करना).
 
 
• *Example - * *After a while her behaviour really began to** irritate me.***
 
 

​​​Thus, the meaning of the underlined idiom i*s **'irritate you'.**.*

Hence,** option (3) **is correct.

questions.question:
What is the meaning of the idiom given below:

'Put your hand to the plough'
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'To set to work'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **idiom **is a group of words established by usage as having a meaning not deducible from those of the individual words__.
 
• **"Put your hand to the plough" **is also an idiom that means __to set to work; to begin or get busy working__.
 
 
• Example: *We've spent a long time planning our study material, and now it's time to put our hand to the plough.*
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 2. **

questions.question:
**Directions: In the following question, four alternatives are given for the idiom/phrase underlined in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

The Social Democratic Party gained votes __at the expense of__ possible allies but lost out to the radical rightist Swedish Democrats.

options.text: To do something in a way that harms or neglects another thing
To spend a lot of money on someone or something, usually one that you don't want to spend
To be careless and jeopardize someone.
To keep somebody unaware of something

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**To do something in a way that harms or neglects another thing**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• If you say that 'someone does something *at the expense of* another thing,' **you are expressing concern at the fact that they are not doing the second thing, ****because the first thing uses all their resources**.
 
• If you achieve 'something at the expense of someone,' **you do it in a way which neglects them or might cause them some harm or disadvantage**.
 
 
• For example, *Divyansh had no need to protect their reputation **at the expense of** his own*.
 
 
 
• So, the correct meaning of the idiom underlined given in the given sentence is '**To do something in a way that harms or neglects another thing**.'

*Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1**.*

questions.question:
**Directions: ****Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom/phrase****.**

Can of worms

options.text: A complicated matter that is likely to prove awkward or embarrassing if pursued.
An attempt that is unlikely to succeed, but may be worth trying.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '__**A **____**complicated matter that is likely to prove awkward or embarrassing if pursued**__.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• 'A can of worms' refers to **a ****situation that causes a lot of problems for you when you start to deal with it**.

 
 
• For example,* Corruption is a serious problem, but nobody has yet been willing to open up that **can of worms***.
 
 
 
• So, the correct meaning of the idiom '*Can of worms*' is '**A complicated matter that is likely to prove awkward or embarrassing if pursued**.'

*Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1**.*

 __

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

It is wise to __sit on the fence__ and not become a party to another World War.

options.text: A person's lack of decisiveness, neutrality or hesitance to choose between two sides in an argument or a competition
Overtaking the thing of interest that the other parties are fighting for while they are fighting
Become a peacemaker between two fighting or competing parties.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"A person's lack of decisiveness, neutrality or hesitance to choose between two sides ****in an argument or a competition"** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 Let's see the given idiom with an example:

__
 
• **Sit on the fence - **to delay making a decision

 
 
• ***Eg. ***You can't* sit on the fence* any longer - you have to decide whose side you're on.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Let's take another similar idiom:

 
• **Sit at the feet of someone -** to be a very admiring student of someone important

 
 
• ***Eg.*** I've been *sitting at the professor's feet *ever since I heard his astounding lecture on quantum mechanics.
 
 
 
• **Sit on a gold mine - **To possess or have access to something that will yield a very large amount of money, especially when that thing has yet to be profited from fully
 
 
• ***Eg.*** If your social networking site is attracting millions of new users every month, then you guys are definitely *sitting on a gold mine.*

questions.question:
**Directions: ****Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom/phrase****.**

Make light of something

options.text: Get off a large vehicle like train, bus etc
Do something that gets you most attention.
Treat something as unimportant or not serious.
To shine a source of light on something

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '__**Treat something as unimportant or not serious.**__.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• 'To make light of someone/ something' is **to act as if something is not serious, esp. when it is serious**.

 
 
• For example, '*Suroj attempted to **make light of **his discomfort*.'
 
 
 
• So, the correct meaning of the idiom '*Make light of something*'*** ***is to **Treat something as unimportant or not serious**.

*Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3**.*
